sources.news_title: Iran Offers Rewards for Killing or Capturing American Soldiers: "Beautiful Women Will Receive a Double Reward
sources.text:
Armata iraniană a anunțat duminică că oferă o recompensă echivalentă cu 30.000 de dolari pentru uciderea sau capturarea soldaților americani, recompensa fiind dublată dacă fapta este comisă de o femeie, relatează France24.
  Șeful armatei, Amir Hatami, a declarat că planul a fost elaborat în urma unui „număr mare de solicitări” de participare, potrivit agenției de știri de stat IRNA.
Nu se cunoaște nicio desfășurare a forțelor terestre americane în Iran pe durata războiului din Orientul Mijlociu, cu excepția unei misiuni de salvare desfășurate în aprilie pentru un pilot american.
Hatami nu a oferit detalii cu privire la locul sau momentul în care se preconiza că vor avea loc uciderea sau capturarea soldaților americani.
  „Oricine ucide sau capturează și predă un membru al personalului militar american invadator va primi o recompensă echivalentă cu 30.000 de dolari sau 5 miliarde de tomani din partea Armatei Republicii Islamice Iran”, a declarat Hatami, folosind o unitate de măsură neoficială echivalentă cu 10.000 de riali iranieni.
„Femeile iraniene curajoase care întreprind o astfel de acțiune vor primi o răsplată dublă”, a adăugat el.
Hatami a reiterat apelul Iranului adresat Statelor Unite de a părăsi Orientul Mijlociu și a declarat că „acestea nu mai au permisiunea de a intra în Golful Persic, în Golful Oman sau în Strâmtoarea Ormuz”. 
Războiul dintre Teheran și Washington a început pe 28 februarie, când Statele Unite și Israelul au atacat Iranul.
La puțin peste o lună de la izbucnirea războiului, Statele Unite au lansat o operațiune de salvare de amploare pentru a-l recupera pe ofițerul responsabil cu sistemele de armament ale unui avion de vânătoare F-15, operațiune la care au participat aproximativ 200 de soldați americani și peste 170 de aeronave, care s-au grăbit să-l găsească pe aviator înaintea forțelor iraniene.
În timpul operațiunii de salvare, trupele iraniene au avariat un avion de atac A-10 care a fost forțat să aterizeze de urgență pe teritoriul aliat. De asemenea, se pare că SUA au abandonat și distrus aeronavele utilizate în cadrul misiunii, inclusiv un avion de transport C-130.
Cu câteva zile înainte, pilotul avionului F-15 fusese salvat de echipajul unui elicopter în cadrul unei operațiuni de mai mică amploare.
Războiul a fost ulterior întrerupt de un armistițiu încheiat în aprilie, după aproape 40 de zile de lupte, urmat de un acord-cadru din iunie privind negocierile de pace, care s-a destrămat ulterior.
De atunci, Iranul și Statele Unite au purtat schimburi sporadice de foc, luptele concentrându-se în principal în sudul Iranului și în jurul Strâmtorii Ormuz.
Contactele indirecte dintre cele două părți, prin intermediul unor mediatori, au continuat, fără a se întrezări vreo perspectivă de progres diplomatic. Iranul a prezentat, de asemenea, o listă de cereri pentru redeschiderea strâmtorii, printre care se numără și despăgubirile pentru pagubele de război.
Numărul militarilor americani uciși de la începutul războiului se ridică la 17, cele mai recente decese având loc în luna iulie. Toți au fost uciși în afara Iranului, în țări precum Iordania și Irak.
Citește și:

     Editor :  A.M.G.

sources.news_title: Iran offers US$30,000 bounty for killing or capturing US soldiers
sources.text:
Iran offers US$30,000 bounty for killing or capturing US soldiers
‘Courageous Iranian women who carry out such an action will receive double the reward,’ said Iran’s army chief Amir Hatami
Iran’s military announced on Sunday that it was offering a bounty equivalent to US$30,000 for killing or capturing US soldiers, with the reward doubled if carried out by a woman.
Army chief Amir Hatami said the plan had been drawn up following a “large number of requests” to take part, according to the IRNA state news agency.
There has been no known deployment of US ground forces in Iran during the Middle East war, with the exception of a rescue mission in April for a downed American airman.
Hatami did not provide any details on where or when the killing or capturing of US soldiers was expected to take place.
“Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to $30,000 or 5 billion tomans from the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Army,” Hatami said, using an informal unit equivalent to 10,000 Iranian rials.
“Courageous Iranian women who carry out such an action will receive double the reward,” he said.
Hatami repeated Iran’s call for the US to leave the Middle East and said “they no longer have permission to enter the Persian Gulf, the Gulf of Oman or the Strait of Hormuz”.

sources.news_title: Iran Announces $30,000 Reward For US Soldiers' Capture Or Killing, Double Bounty For Women
sources.text:
Iran Announces $30,000 Reward For US Soldiers' Capture Or Killing, Double Bounty For Women
Iran has offered a bounty to those who manage to capture or kill a US military personnel and bring them before the authorities, says the state-run media of Iran.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
Amir Hatami, the commander-in-chief of the Iranian Army, announced that the value of the bounty is to be $30,000, or 5 billion Iranian tomans. Women will get two times more money if they accomplish the task.
The declaration comes at a time when Iran and the US are still at odds, while the Strait of Hormuz continues to be the main problem in achieving a compromise solution.
Iran Announces Reward For US Military Personnel
Iran's official news agency IRNA says that Hatami stated that the offer was made after having received many applications from individuals who wanted to help in the financing of Iran's war effort.
According to the announcement, an individual who kidnaps an American military personnel and turns him or her over to Iran will be paid the offered reward. The same reward will be provided for an individual who murders an American military personnel.
No location was specified by Hatami as to where the event may take place.
No large US military ground force has also been deployed within Iran since the start of the conflict. An American rescue operation had previously been carried out after an American plane had been shot down.
Women Offered Twice The Amount
Hatami separately announced a higher reward for women.
He said an Iranian woman who captures a US military personnel and hands them over would receive double the standard bounty.
The announcement adds another unusual element to the ongoing confrontation between the two countries.
Why The Strait Of Hormuz Matters
The Strait of Hormuz continues to be one of the biggest issues in the confrontation between Iran and the US.
The narrow waterway connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and is one of the world's most important routes for energy shipments.
Any prolonged disruption in the strait can affect oil and gas supplies, shipping costs and energy prices across international markets.
The status of the waterway has therefore become closely linked to diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions in the region.
How The US-Iran Conflict Escalated
The war started on February 28, as attacks against Iranian targets were initiated by the United States and Israel, as described in the article.
Iran retaliated with attacks against Israeli and American military forces stationed in other countries.
The war then progressed to alternating phases of war, ceasefire, and peace negotiations.
However, disagreements regarding security, military and the Strait of Hormuz have impeded progress toward finding an amicable resolution.
Commercial Shipping Also Caught In The Conflict
The conflict has had consequences beyond military targets.
Commercial shipping has faced disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, while attacks involving Yemen's Houthi rebels have also affected shipping routes in and around the Red Sea.
The resulting uncertainty has increased concerns about maritime security, energy supplies and the cost of transporting goods.

sources.news_title: Iran offers $30,000 bounty for killing, capturing U.S. soldiers
sources.text:
Iran's military announced on Sunday (August 16, 2026) that it was offering a bounty equivalent to $30,000 for killing or capturing U.S. soldiers, with the reward doubled if carried out by a woman.
Aslo Read: West Asia war updates on August 16
Army chief Amir Hatami said the plan had been drawn up following a "large number of requests" to participate, according to the IRNA state news agency.
There has been no known deployment of U.S. ground forces in Iran during the West Asia war, except for a rescue mission in April for a downed American airman.
Mr. Hatami did not provide any details on where or when the killing or capturing of US soldiers was expected to take place.
"Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to $30,000 or 5 billion tomans from the Islamic Republic of Iran's Army," Mr. Hatami said, using an informal unit equivalent to 10,000 Iranian rials.
"Courageous Iranian women who carry out such an action will receive double the reward," he added.
Mr. Hatami repeated Iran's call for the U.S. to leave West Asia, and said: "They no longer have permission to enter the Persian Gulf, the Gulf of Oman or the Strait of Hormuz".
The war between Tehran and Washington began on February 28 when the United States and Israel attacked Iran.
Just over a month into the war, the U.S. launched a massive rescue operation to retrieve the weapon systems officer of an F-15 jet, involving around 200 U.S. troops and more than 170 aircraft racing to find the airman ahead of Iranian forces.
During the rescue, Iranian troops damaged an A-10 ground attack aircraft, which was ditched over friendly territory. The U.S. also reportedly abandoned and destroyed aircraft used during the mission including a C-130 transport plane.
Days before, the pilot of the F-15 was rescued by a helicopter crew in a smaller operation. The war was later paused by an April ceasefire after nearly 40 days of fighting, followed by a June framework for peace talks that later collapsed.
Iran and the United States have since traded fire sporadically, with fighting mainly centred in southern Iran and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Indirect contact between the two sides via mediators has continued with little sign of any diplomatic breakthrough. Iran has also set out a list of demands for reopening the strait, including war damages.
The number of U.S. military personnel killed since the start of the war stands at 17, with the most recent deaths in July. They have all been killed outside of Iran, in countries including Jordan and Iraq.

sources.news_title: Financial Jihad: Iran to offer $30,000 bounty for killing, capturing US soldiers
sources.text:
Financial Jihad: Iran offers $30,000 bounty for killing, capturing US soldiers
The Iranian Army chief also claimed that the conflict has shattered Washington's military dominance and prompted countries to explore other ways of ensuring their security.
Iran’s military has announced a $30,000 bounty for anyone who kills or captures a US soldier, with the reward doubled if the act is carried out by a woman, Iranian state media reported on Sunday.
Iranian Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami said the plan was drawn up after numerous requests from people seeking to support the country's war efforts via “financial jihad”.
“Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to $30,000, or 5 billion tomans, from the Islamic Republic of Iran Army,” Hatami said during a speech in Tehran.
He further said “courageous Iranian women” who carry out such an act will receive double the amount.
Hatami also said the weapon used by anyone who killed a US soldier would be purchased for twice its value and replaced with a new one. The original weapon would be preserved in a proposed museum, he added.
Hatami, however, did not clarify where or when Iranian fighters were expected to encounter US personnel.
There has been no known deployment of American ground forces in Iran during the conflict, apart from an April mission to rescue a downed US pilot.
HATAMI TARGETS US, PRESIDENT TRUMP
The Iranian Army chief also claimed that the conflict has shattered Washington’s military dominance and prompted countries to explore other ways of ensuring their security.
“America no longer has the authority it once had,” The Jerusalem Post quoted Hatami as saying.
Hatami also criticised US President Donald Trump’s statement that the Strait of Hormuz would be declared a “territory of the United States” after Iran’s defeat.
He accused Trump of trying to project victory despite what he described as America’s weakened global standing.
The Iranian Commander-in-Chief also threatened US bases in West Asia, saying Tehran would not permit facilities that posed a threat to Iran to resume operations in neighbouring countries.
According to The Jerusalem Post, Hatami claimed that American forces had effectively been driven out and were no longer permitted to enter the Persian Gulf, the Sea of Oman or the Strait of Hormuz.
The announcement comes as efforts to begin peace talks remain stalled and oil tanker traffic through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz continues to face disruption.
Hatami’s remarks offered no indication that the warring sides were moving towards ending the conflict launched by the US and Israel on February 28.

sources.news_title: 'Courageous Iranian Women' Offered Double $30,000 Bounty to Kill or Capture Invading US Personnel
sources.text:
'Courageous Iranian Women' Offered Double $30,000 Bounty to Kill or Capture Invading US Personnel
Tehran's new incentive scheme targets American military personnel
Iran's military announced on Sunday that it is offering a reward equivalent to $30,000 (£22,200) to anyone who kills or captures a US service member, with the bounty doubled to $60,000 (£44,300) if the act is carried out by an Iranian woman.
For context, the offer comes amid a protracted and unpredictable conflict between Washington and Tehran in the Middle East. Both sides have traded intermittent strikes, while diplomatic efforts have largely stalled. Disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz and other provisions of an interim agreement have repeatedly complicated attempts to secure a lasting peace since full-scale hostilities first erupted on 28 February.
Double Rewards Target US Service Members
According to Iranian state media, Iranian Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami confirmed the new financial incentive scheme. Hatami explained that the military command established the reward structure after receiving numerous requests from members of the public seeking to contribute financially to the war effort.
'Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to $30,000 (£22,200), or 5 billion tomans, from the Islamic Republic of Iran's Army,' Hatami said. The toman is an informal Iranian currency unit equivalent to 10 rials.
Hatami went on to specify that Iranian women would receive twice the baseline payout if they managed to capture or kill US personnel. 'Courageous Iranian women who carry out such an action will receive double the reward,' Hatami added.
Bounty Offered for Capturing US Personnel
It remains unclear how the programme would operate in practice. Hatami provided no operational details regarding exactly where or when such killings or captures were anticipated to take place. Reporting on the announcement similarly noted that he did not specify where such encounters might occur.
There has been no large-scale publicly confirmed deployment of American ground troops inside Iranian territory during the current conflict. Much of the US campaign has instead involved air and naval operations, including an American blockade of Iranian shipping.
The financial incentive highlights how Tehran is attempting to project domestic resistance against US forces. The military leadership is publicising the cash rewards even though opportunities for Iranian civilians to encounter American personnel directly appear limited.
Tensions Rise Over Blockaded Strait of Hormuz
The broader conflict started on 28 February when the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes against Iran, targeting its nuclear and ballistic missile programmes and seeking regime change, according to US and Israeli statements.
Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed during the opening strikes. Tehran responded with attacks against Israel, US military bases in the region and sites in neighbouring Middle Eastern states.
Tehran subsequently closed the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington imposed a naval blockade on Iranian shipping. Because roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption passes through the waterway, the disruption put significant pressure on global energy markets and the wider economy. Commercial traffic through the strait remains sharply reduced amid renewed tensions.
Sporadic Fighting Continues Around Iran and the Gulf
An April ceasefire temporarily reduced hostilities, although intermittent fighting resumed in May. Iran and the United States later signed a separate Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June aimed at ending hostilities and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
That agreement subsequently unravelled. Trump declared it 'over' on 7 July, while Iran later suspended the deal and halted direct military and diplomatic engagement with Washington. Efforts by mediators including Pakistan and Qatar to revive it have so far made little progress.
Since then, Iran and the United States have continued periods of confrontation punctuated by pauses in military activity. The Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters remain a central flashpoint, with shipping traffic disrupted and both sides accusing the other of violating previous agreements.
Meanwhile, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have carried out attacks on commercial shipping and other regional targets. Recent attacks around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait have added another layer of instability to maritime routes already affected by the US-Iran conflict.

sources.text:
Iran has been taking a pounding from the United States and Israel for some months now. The regime is battered; the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps now appears to be either in charge or angling to be, having already seized control of what's left of Iran's military. Their civil leadership has been reduced to the third level by American explosives. And, the country is broke, with inflation at astronomic levels and their ports blockaded by the United States Navy.
So, when you hear that Iran is now offering a bounty to whomever can kill or capture an American service member, said bounty amounting to five billion tomans, about $30,000 in American freedom dollars, you have to wonder where they think they'll get the money should someone seek to collect. A toman is a superunit of Iran's rial, amounting to 10,000 of the new, devalued rials. Oh, and if a woman claims the prize, the award is doubled.

What's left of Iran's leadership may be trying to get by on the cheap, but here's the real flaw in this notion: There are no American service members on the ground in Iran. That means anyone seeking this bounty would have to carry out their attack somewhere else, such as on an American installation elsewhere in the Middle East, and that's not going to be an easy task for an Iranian man (or woman) with his (or her) eye on the main chance. Add to that the complication of anyone collecting on this if they are not in Iran. How are they to get paid, when so much of Iran's remaining assets are locked up? It's not like Iran can take a page from Barack Obama's book and airlift a pallet of Iranian cash to some goblin hiding in the sand dunes in Kuwait.
An announcement like this smacks of desperation. This isn't an offer made by a regime that's confident about their chances of prevailing.
Then again, we are forced to remember, there are an unknown number of Iranian nationals illegally in the United States right now, in large part because of four years of non-enforcement of our borders and our immigration laws under Joe Biden, and we have little idea where many of them are and what they may be up to. That, honestly, is the real elephant in the room.

This comes amid continued tensions between Iran and the US in West Asia, with the two occasionally trading strikes on each other's interests in the region. The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz has been a continuous hurdle in any peace deal since the war began on February 28.

"Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to $30,000 or 5 billion tomans from the Islamic Republic of Iran's Army," Hatami was quoted by IRNA as saying, using an informal unit equivalent to 10,000 Iranian rials.
Hatami also announced that the bounty will be doubled if the capture is carried out by a woman.
"Courageous Iranian women who carry out such an action will receive double the reward," he added.
The US-Iran tensions in West Asia

Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed on the first day of the war, with Tehran retaliating with strikes on Israel and various US bases in neighbouring Arab countries.
Iran also put an effective blockade on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway through which about a fifth of the world’s oil and gas passes. This sent the oil and gas prices soaring and the global economy into a tailspin.
The initial attacks were followed by an April ceasefire, brokered by Pakistan, after nearly 40 days of fighting, and a June framework for peace talks that later collapsed.
